target_customer: Developers and agent users who run open models locally on Apple Silicon, NVIDIA, AMD or CPU.
problem: Local inference engines are not tuned to each machine, so open models run slower than the hardware allows.
business_model: Open source (Apache 2.0) desktop app and engine; monetization not stated
product_category: Local inference engine for open models

founders.name: Tom Greenwald
founders.background_notes: Ran special projects as a product manager at SimpliSafe per YC page.

founders.name: Anders Lie
education: Iowa State University, Computer Science and Math
founders.background_notes: Software engineer on no-code automation at AWS per YC page.

competitors.name: Browser Use
competitors.what: Open source web agents (YC W25); rival to Magnitude's original browser agent

technical_complexity.rationale: Self-tuning kernels per device, speculative decoding and quantized KV caches across several hardware backends for a two person team.

defensibility.rationale: Open source with strong incumbents (llama.cpp, Ollama, MLX, LM Studio); performance lead can be copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Comparison articles in 2026 show these runtimes improving, including Ollama adopting MLX; no acquisition of Magnitude found.

market_need_then: Original browser agent launched on Show HN in mid 2025 and claimed 94 percent on WebVoyager; the inference pivot launched 2026-09-30 claiming over 2x faster than Ollama (company claims).

identity.voice_and_tone: Minimal, text focused, performance claims (company site).

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word shared with an unrelated cybersecurity startup and other firms; no brand press found.

pivots.from: Open source vision-first browser agent and web app testing framework
pivots.to: Coding agent for open models, then a self-tuning local inference engine launched 2026-09
pivots.why: Not stated by the company in sources found.

outcome_analysis: Magnitude began as an open source browser agent in the Summer 2025 batch and by September 2026 had shifted to a local inference engine, facing entrenched open source runtimes. No funding or exit is verified, so the outcome is unknown and the repeated pivots are the main signal.
notes: The 10M seed led by Ballistic Ventures belongs to a different cybersecurity company named Magnitude. Pivot dates are approximate: the browser agent Show HN was about mid 2025 per an HN mirror; the coding agent step comes from one aggregator listing. Inference competitors (Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX, LM Studio) are as of 2026, not founding, so are not in the competitor list.
